questions.q: Why does Oracle require validation of an AAD before it can be used?
options: Validation is optional and rarely performed in practice
Because configuration built by a person across many screens can contain gaps, like an incomplete account rule, that validation is designed to catch before live processing
Validation only checks spelling in descriptions
Validation replaces the need for account rules entirely
questions.explain: Validation automatically checks an AAD's structure for completeness and consistency to catch configuration gaps before they affect real transactions.

questions.q: What is the difference between validation and activation?
options: They are two names for the exact same step
Activation happens first, then validation
Validation only applies to Receivables AADs
Validation confirms the definition is structurally sound; activation is the separate step that makes a validated AAD usable by Create Accounting
questions.explain: Validation checks structural soundness; activation is a distinct, later step that makes an already-validated AAD available for live use.

questions.q: Can an AAD be activated if it has not passed validation?
options: Yes, activation and validation are unrelated
No — Oracle will not allow an AAD to be activated unless it has successfully passed validation
Only with special administrator override, with no restrictions
Yes, but only for Fixed Assets AADs
questions.explain: Oracle enforces the order: an AAD must pass validation before it can be activated for live use.

questions.q: In the worked example, what gap would validation be expected to flag?
options: A perfectly fine account rule with no issues
A missing Chart of Accounts
An account rule for Freight lines with a condition for Domestic freight but no fallback condition for other categories like International
A ledger with no currency assigned
questions.explain: The example account rule only handled the Domestic freight category, with no default/fallback condition for any other category, which validation is designed to catch.

questions.q: Why is it considered better for a gap to be caught during validation rather than discovered later?
options: It isn't better; timing makes no difference
Validation cannot actually catch any real issues
Because validation deletes the problematic transaction automatically
Because catching it during a controlled setup session is far less disruptive than a controller discovering a transaction that silently failed to account correctly weeks later
questions.explain: Catching configuration gaps during setup avoids the much costlier scenario of a real transaction failing to account correctly in production.
